A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rpoA, rpoB, recA, hsp65 and 16S genes were all useful for phylogenetic studies of the RGM, but the rpoB gene was the most appropriate for delineating phylogenetic relationships.

the M. cheloane-abscessus, the M. mucogenium and the M. fortutium groups are the main groups of RGM, the M. margetense group being an emerging group and the M wolinskyi group being the most divergent.

the phylogenetic organization of RGM species based on the combined datasets of the 16 S rRNA and rpoB genes and the combined datasets of 16S r RNA, rpoB+ recA genes is more robust than the phylogenetic organizations based on the 16S RNA, hsp65 or sodA gene sequences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rpoB and, to a lesser extent, recA gene sequences are useful for phylogenetic studies of RGM species.
rpoB and rpoB+ recA gene sequences are useful in delineating phylogenetic relationships within rapidly growing mycobacterial species.
the rpo B and rec A genes, in addition to the hsp 65 and sod A genes, are useful tools for the study of phylogenetic relationship among RGM species.
